dedupe_keys.name: esa anomaly detection benchmark esa adb annotated satellite telemetry

description: ESA-ADB is the first large, real-world dataset of satellite housekeeping telemetry with anomalies marked by the engineers who operate the spacecraft, released in 2024 by the European Space Agency's operations centre with Airbus Defence and Space and the Polish firm KP Labs under ESA's artificial intelligence for automation roadmap. The ESA Anomalies Dataset holds about 31 GB of multivariate telemetry from three ESA missions, anonymised, with curated annotations of events; two missions form the benchmark, which reports 844 annotated events of which 148 are classed as anomalies. The benchmark adds an evaluation pipeline and metrics designed with operators so that machine learning detectors are judged by what matters in operations, such as timely alarms and few false positives, and the accompanying paper, first posted in June 2024 and revised in August 2025, compares existing detection methods on it. Coverage: three ESA missions over several years of operations. Format and access: data on Zenodo and code on GitHub, free and publicly available. Caveats: missions and channels are anonymised, so physical interpretation is limited; annotations reflect one agency's practice. Simulation uses: training and testing anomaly detectors for satellite operations, failure and degradation models of spacecraft subsystems, and digital twins of satellite fleets. Related records: the NOAA satellite anomaly archive and Seradata record anomalies across many operators without telemetry.
